title: Generators & Iterators
definition: Generators are special functions that can be paused and resumed, allowing them to yield multiple values one by one, on demand. They are defined using the `function*` syntax and the `yield` keyword.
simpleExplanation: A normal function runs from top to bottom without stopping. A generator is like a function with a pause button. It does some work, spits out a value (yield), and pauses. When you ask it for the next value, it unpauses, does a bit more work, spits out the next value, and pauses again.
realWorldExample: If you need to generate a massive list of numbers (like an infinite sequence of IDs), a regular function would crash because it tries to build the infinite array in memory. A generator only calculates one ID at a time exactly when you ask for it.
useCases: Managing infinite data streams without running out of memory
Implementing custom iterables (objects you can use in a `for...of` loop)
Managing complex asynchronous flows (used heavily by Redux Saga)

answers.question: What does calling a generator function return?
answers.answer: Calling a generator function doesn't execute the code inside it right away. Instead, it returns a special Iterator object. You must call `.next()` on that object to start execution.

answers.question: Can you pass data back INTO a paused generator?
answers.answer: Yes. When you call `iterator.next(value)`, the value you pass in is returned by the currently paused `yield` expression inside the generator.

answers.question: What happens if you use `return` inside a generator?
answers.answer: It finishes the generator immediately. The returned object will look like `{ value: yourReturnValue, done: true }`. Subsequent calls to `.next()` will yield `{ value: undefined, done: true }`.
